result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.all_pairs_shortest_path_length()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Compute shortest path lengths for all pairs of nodes. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L22487-L22560){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.all_pairs_shortest_path_length() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![All-pairs shortest path lengths](/assets/graphs/all-pairs-shortest-path-length.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="A four-node directed weighted cycle A, B, C, D with a direct shortcut A to C of weight 4. The distance matrix lists every source-target cost; the highlighted cell A to C is 3, because the route through B (1 + 2, in the accent color) beats the direct edge." width="100%"} Uses Dijkstra's algorithm from each source node to find the shortest path distance to all other reachable nodes. For unweighted graphs, all edges are treated as having weight `1.0`. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [dict[int, dict[int, float]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Nested dictionary where `result[source][target] = distance`. Only includes reachable pairs. Unreachable pairs are omitted. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Runs Dijkstra from every node, giving $O(n(m + n)\log n)$ time and $O(n^2)$ space to hold the full distance matrix. Unreachable pairs simply do not appear in the result, so the returned dict may be sparse for disconnected or directed graphs. On graphs where individual queries are the whole workload, calling `shortest_path()` on demand is usually cheaper; the payoff of computing everything up-front is when many pairs are needed or when the same distances feed several downstream metrics. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Simple path graph: ::: {#7953b8ca .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph() graph.add_path_graph(4) # Creates 1-2-3-4 distances = graph.all_pairs_shortest_path_length() distances[1][4], distances[2][4] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (3.0, 2.0) ``` ::: ::: Weighted graph: ::: {#667fa9d3 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph(weighted=True) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_edge(source="A", target="B", weight=1.0) .add_edge(source="B", target="C", weight=2.0) .add_edge(source="A", target="C", weight=5.0) ) distances = graph.all_pairs_shortest_path_length() a_id = graph.get_id_from_label("A") c_id = graph.get_id_from_label("C") # A->B->C (total 3.0) is shorter than the direct A->C edge (5.0) distances[a_id][c_id] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 3.0 ``` ::: ::: Disconnected components: ::: {#72e57880 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph() graph.add_path_graph(3) # 1-2-3 graph.add_node(4) # Isolated node distances = graph.all_pairs_shortest_path_length() 1 in distances, 4 in distances[1] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` (True, False) ``` ::: :::
